# Cantrip.Linting

The linter, and every diagnostic code it can report, each as a named constant.

Part of [the API reference](README.md). The guides are [docs/csharp.md](../csharp.md) and [docs/godot.md](../godot.md); when something here surprises you, [docs/troubleshooting.md](../troubleshooting.md) is the other end of it.

| Type | |
|---|---|
| [`LintOptions`](#lintoptions) | Tunes a lint run for a particular game. |
| [`Linter`](#linter) | Static checks over loaded content: mistakes that would otherwise only show up when the effect runs, if ever. The linter never executes content, so it is safe to run in editors and CI on anything, including content that does not load cleanly. |

## LintOptions

```csharp
public sealed class LintOptions
```

Tunes a lint run for a particular game.

### Properties

```csharp
public ISet<string> HostBlocks { get; }
```

Blocks the game runs itself, reading them from C# through `EntityDefinition.Blocks`, such as a custom `on_reveal:`. The engine runs only `effect:` and `move ...:`.

```csharp
public ISet<string> HostEvents { get; }
```

Events the game raises from C#.

```csharp
public ISet<string> HostNames { get; }
```

Names the game's `IEffectHost` resolves, and stats it only sets from C#.

```csharp
public ISet<string> HostVerbs { get; }
```

Verbs the game registers from C# with `RegisterVerb`.

```csharp
public ISet<string> Suppressed { get; }
```

Diagnostic codes to leave out, such as `CT306`.

## Linter

```csharp
public sealed class Linter
```

Static checks over loaded content: mistakes that would otherwise only show up when the effect runs, if ever. The linter never executes content, so it is safe to run in editors and CI on anything, including content that does not load cleanly.

### Fields and constants

```csharp
public const string AbilityCost = "CT339"
```

`cost` on an ability. An ability is paid for in the seconds it makes you wait; nothing spends the resource a `cost` line names, so the number reads like a rule and is not one.

```csharp
public const string PlayerWhereAMemberIsMeant = "CT326"
```

`player` written where a party member is meant. It is an error rather than a warning because the alternative is a party game whose every enemy move hits one hero forever, silently — and a silent wrong answer is the one class of change this project has a written policy against.

```csharp
public const string ScenarioWithoutTurns = "CT338"
```

A `scenario` in a game that says `clock ticks`. The simulator plays a scenario by taking turns, and a real-time game has none, so every number it printed was about a game nobody played.

```csharp
public const string ScopeCannotMatch = "CT336"
```

An `of` group that can never hold the one the value belongs to: a pile of cards on a channel that belongs to an actor. A modifier that cannot match is worth saying out loud rather than leaving to a test that guessed the number.

```csharp
public const string TurnMachineryWithoutTurns = "CT337"
```

Turn machinery written into a game that says `clock ticks`. CT325 checks the *units* a designer writes; this checks the *declarations*. A `move`, a `pattern`, a `phase`, a `stacking duration`, a `decay ... on turn_end`, an `until turn_end:`, a `next turn:`, an `once per turn`, a `reset_on turn_start` and a `turn_start` listener are every one of them driven by a turn, and a real-time game takes none.

Before this, content whose ruleset said `clock ticks` and which declared moves, patterns and phases that could never run linted with zero errors, zero warnings and zero notes, while a `2 turns` in the same file was CT325. The language checked the unit an author wrote and not the machinery they used, so half the vocabulary was silently inert: `apply Chill 3` on a tick clock was a permanent Chill.

```csharp
public const string TurnOrderWithoutTurns = "CT335"
```

A turn order written into a game whose clock has no turns. CT334 was the `turns:` and `order:` values the first party release had not built yet; both are built, and a value nothing recognises is already CT0202, so the code was retired rather than re-used.
